transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Thank you. Well, I came in because my sleep has just been completely thrown off lately. I’m usually a very disciplined sleeper, but... since my cousin died, I just lie awake replaying that night. And when I do finally drift off, I end up waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning from these scraps of hospital images in my head. It's incredibly frustrating. I'm having to go into my board meetings feeling like I’ve only slept in pieces.
How many days or weeks has it been since your cousin passed away, and how long have you been having these sleep problems since then?
It's been about three weeks. She died in a highway collision, and... well, the sleep problems started right after that night. So, yes, this has all been going on for about three weeks now.
Besides at night, do you find yourself having unwanted memories or images of the accident intruding during the day, or actively avoiding reminders of it?

Yes, I do. It happens at odd moments during the day. Like, if I hear a phone ring unexpectedly, or if I'm driving and see the glare of headlights on the highway... suddenly, this very sharp picture of the hospital corridor just pushes into my mind. Or I'll hear the police officer's voice from that night. It just kind of intrudes, and I have to pause for a second to steady myself before I can get back to what I was doing.
Since the accident, have you noticed feeling unusually jumpy, on edge, or easily startled—more than before?

Yes, I have been feeling more on edge, especially when I'm in the car. When I drive now, I keep checking the mirrors constantly, watching the speed of the trucks around me, always looking for where I could pull off if I needed to. Even just taking the familiar roads to the office, my body stays completely tight... it's like I’m just waiting for something bad to happen. It's definitely more than I ever used to.
Have you found yourself deliberately avoiding certain places, people, activities, or conversations that remind you of the accident?

No, I haven't really done that. I mean, I still drive the same routes to the office, even though it makes me tense, like I said. And... I haven't stopped talking to my family about her or the accident. We had to handle all the funeral arrangements, so avoiding those conversations wasn't really an option anyway. I've mostly just kept going with my normal routine as best as I can.

Since the accident, have you had moments where you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings—like you were in a daze, watching things happen from outside your body, or like things around you didn't feel real?

No, I haven't really felt anything like that. I mean, I'm definitely stressed and on edge, but I always feel like I'm... in my own body, you know? Things feel real, just... harder to deal with right now. But I haven't felt detached or in a daze like you're describing.

Since the accident, have you noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling persistently guilty, blaming yourself or others, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling more distant from friends or family?

Well, I wouldn't say I feel guilty or blame anyone. But... I have noticed a change in how I feel around my family, which I guess you could call feeling distant. 

During the prayer gatherings we had, and even when my nieces were trying to comfort me, I found myself just going through the motions. I was behaving properly and saying the right things, but... I just wasn't feeling any warmth or relief inside. It's almost as if the affectionate part of me has just gone quiet. I'm there with them, but I just can't seem to feel those positive emotions right now.

Since the accident, have these symptoms—the intrusive memories, sleep problems, and feeling on edge—been constant and unchanging every day, or have you noticed any days where they started to ease up before coming back?

They've been pretty constant, really. I haven't noticed them easing up at all. This has been going on every day for about three weeks now, ever since the night my cousin died in that highway collision.
Just to pin down the timeline precisely—counting from the night of the accident to today, has it been exactly three weeks, or could it actually be closer to four weeks or more?
Let me think... no, it hasn't been four weeks. It's been right at three weeks. Maybe three weeks and a day or two, but definitely not a month yet.
